title: The descended omega is the exceptional image of the actual coefficient unit
statement: Fix D,l,Omega,X as in [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], and let B be any of its normalized Dualities. There exists an Exceptional A at the canonical integralDualizingCompactification of the structure morphism such that B.omega is isomorphic to A.right applied to the actual base-stage coefficientUnit, and for every finite coefficient field E, RationalOperations.DualizingIdentification holds for A.system and B.finite.omega E. Thus the unchanged predicate Dualizing B holds, with the same exceptional system at every finite field.

proof.text: Apply core_descent at Spec(k), then completeCore, to obtain the base duality. Apply exceptional_descent to the given B and this base duality at the structure morphism and integralDualizingCompactification. Keep its Exceptional A; the exceptional-formula witness is not needed for this assertion.

Apply rationalDualizing_identification to this same A.system, the auxiliary small closure and each fieldStage E, with the given B.finite.omega E. Its universal quantification over normalized systems and coherent dualizing data gives every required finite DualizingIdentification directly.

Take E = finiteCoefficientBase. Reverse B.omegaComparison E, compose with the image under inclusion E of the finite isomorphism from the preceding step, and then with (A.rightComparison E).app at the rational coefficientUnit. By the definitions of coefficientUnit and finiteRight, the endpoints are exactly B.omega and A.right.obj of the actual base-stage coefficientUnit. These three isomorphisms give the required Nonempty; pair it with the full finite family from the preceding step.
